Key Takeaway: FGSM: one-step attack x_adv = x + eps*sign(grad of loss wrt x). Argues adversarial examples come from models being too linear in high dimensions (not nonlinearity or overfitting), so tiny per-pixel changes add up. Adversarial examples transfer across models because they learn similar linear directions. Mixing clean and FGSM examples in training (alpha=0.5) regularizes and cuts FGSM error from 89.4% to 17.9% on MNIST. Ensembles and random noise do not help.

Paper: Benchmarking Neural Network Robustness to Common Corruptions and Perturbations (CIFAR-10-C)
Are Transformers More Robust Than CNNs?
Fast is better than free: Revisiting adversarial training
Robustness May Be at Odds with Accuracy
Theoretically Principled Trade-off between Robustness and Accuracy (TRADES)
Key Takeaway: Splits robust error into natural error plus boundary error and trains with cross-entropy plus beta times KL(clean vs adversarial output). Beta controls the trade-off: with WRN-34-10 at eps 0.031, beta 1 gives 88.64% clean and about 49% robust, beta 6 gives 84.92% clean and 56.61% robust.

Paper: Towards Deep Learning Models Resistant to Adversarial Attacks (PGD)
Key Takeaway: Frames robustness as a min-max problem and uses multi-step PGD (L-inf, eps 8/255) as both the attack and the inner step of adversarial training. Robustness needs larger model capacity. PGD-trained CIFAR-10 model reaches about 87% clean and about 46% under PGD-20.

Paper: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Neural Networks (C&W)
Key Takeaway: Optimization-based L0, L2 and Linf attacks that minimize perturbation size plus c times a logit-margin loss, with tanh change of variables and binary search on c. Broke defensive distillation with 100% success, showing that failing weak attacks does not mean a model is robust.

Paper: Reliable evaluation of adversarial robustness with an ensemble of diverse parameter-free attacks (AutoAttack)
Key Takeaway: Ensemble of APGD-CE, APGD-T with DLR loss, FAB-T and Square needing no tuning. PGD with fixed step size and cross-entropy overestimates robustness; AutoAttack lowered reported robust accuracy for almost all of 50+ models, by over 10% for 13 of them. Use it as the minimal final test.
